I am 47 and I've been farming these 36 mu for 30 years. Never went to school, so I don't read those extension pamphlets — I go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the old farmers in the village do. My husband and my oldest son work at a factory in the county town, so it's mostly me and my daughter-in-law in the fields. They send money home, which helps me buy seeds and fertilizer, but it also means fewer hands at harvest, especially for the cotton picking.

I have 18 mu in wheat that I planted last October right after the maize came off. The wheat is already up, and now at the start of the growing season I need to topdress it with urea when it starts jointing — I never skip this. Two years ago when the spring turned dry, my neighbor Wang who didn't topdress barely got 200 jin per mu. I put about half a bag of urea per mu, around 20 kg, and I irrigate three times total for the wheat. I use the improved wheat seed from the county store, not the old kind.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, the window to plant summer maize is only two or three days. I buy new hybrid maize seed every year — 60 yuan a bag — and I plant fast, usually no-till or one quick pass with the rotary tiller if the stubble is too thick. I put compound fertilizer in the seed furrow at planting, about 25 kg per mu, and if the plants look yellow at jointing I topdress with another 15 kg of urea. I irrigate maize twice; if the summer rains are good I might skip the second watering.

My 14 mu of cotton is the hardest work. I buy hybrid cotton seed because saved seed gets weak and doesn't make bolls. I plow in early spring and harrow before planting in mid-to-late April. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 30 kg per mu, then urea at flowering, about 15 kg per mu. Last year I got greedy and put too much fertilizer — the cotton grew tall like trees but barely made bolls. I wasted money. This year I'm sticking to what I know: 13 kg nitrogen per mu, no more. Cotton needs a lot of spraying for bollworms and leaf diseases, so I hire the sprayer from the village. I irrigate three times. At harvest I hire women from the village to help pick; 14 mu is too much for just me and my daughter-in-law.

I keep 4 mu of mungbean because it's easy money and fixes the soil a bit. I plant in mid-May with seed I saved from last year — why buy new seed for mungbean? I put a small handful of compound fertilizer in the furrow, about 10 kg per mu, water once, spray herbicide once, and harvest in late August. It doesn't make much, but it's reliable.

All together I'll spend about 16,500 yuan on inputs this year. That's a lot, but I'd rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk a drought like 2019, when the corn that got less fertilizer barely made ears. I don't want that again.
